$comment: Single source of truth for what every security scan treats as a failure.
Read by scripts/security-audit.mjs and security/tests/*.spec.ts. Changing a
threshold here changes the gate; it is deliberately not spread across tool
invocations. See security/docs/security-exceptions.md for the process that
governs waiving an individual finding rather than lowering a threshold.
Issue #45 item 9.
The full dependency tree is gated, not just production. The RN/Expo
toolchain is a dev dependency but its output is what ships, so a compromise
there is a compromise of the artifact.
Findings at or above failOn must each carry a waiver in
security/config/audit-waivers.json. Anything new fails immediately.
Lockfile scan via scripts/security-osv.mjs. osv-scanner has no severity
threshold of its own -- it exits non-zero on any finding -- so the wrapper
applies this one and honours the npm-audit waiver register, giving one
advisory one decision recorded in one place.
failOn is a qualitative CVSS v3 rating: CRITICAL is >= 9.0.
Custom rules in security/config/semgrep.yml plus the registry packs.
ERROR-severity rules are defects and block. WARNING-severity rules point at
work to do -- they are reported but do not stop a push, because a gate that
cries wolf gets bypassed.
A ratchet, not a target. Warnings may only ever go down. Lower this number
as cleanup lands; never raise it to accommodate new warnings.
Issue #45 item 3.
gitleaks. `required` means the pre-push hook fails when the binary is
absent rather than printing a note and continuing -- a gate that silently
skips is not a gate. Issue #45 item 7.
Enforced by security/tests/workflows.security.spec.ts rather than by adding
a scanner binary: it runs in the existing `npm test` gate, needs no install,
and works offline. Issue #45 items 4-6.
